standard_prerequisites.name: Local finiteness of the irreducible components of a closed subscheme, finiteness of multiplicities, specialisation of points and finiteness of length over a ring whose module is supported at the closed point
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Divisors, label divisors-lemma-components-locally-finite (proof line 1728); Same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-multiplicity-finite (proof line 1730); Schemes, label schemes-lemma-specialize-points (proof line 1737); Algebra, label algebra-lemma-support-point (proof line 1740)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first two give parts (1) and (3) directly, and the last two show that the stalk at the generic point is a finite module over a local ring supported only at the closed point, hence of finite length.

core_obligations: Reduce to the support: the support is closed, so view it as a reduced closed subscheme, from which the local finiteness of the components (part 1) and the statement about points of maximal dimension (part 3) follow by the corresponding statements for a closed subscheme (proof lines 1722-1730).

Analyse the stalk at the generic point: for a point of an irreducible component the stalks at all specialising points vanish, and the non-maximal primes of the local ring correspond to those specialising points, so the stalk is a finite module over the local ring supported only at its closed point (proof lines 1732-1739).
Conclude finite length by the criterion for a module supported at the closed point of a local ring (proof line 1740).
proof_roadmap: Support as a reduced closed subscheme and parts (1), (3) (proof lines 1722-1730).
Vanishing of the nearby stalks and support at the closed point (proof lines 1732-1739).
Finite length by the criterion (proof line 1740).
difficulty_reason: The lemma records three facts about the support of a coherent module: its irreducible components are locally finite, the length of the stalk at the generic point of a component is finite, and a point where the dimension function attains the maximal value on the support is a generic point of a component (statement lines 1701-1720, tag 02QH-adjacent). The first and third are deduced from the corresponding statements for a reduced closed subscheme, and the second requires the observation that the nearby stalks vanish so that the stalk is supported at the closed point of a local ring, hence of finite length. That vanishing argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.
